_comment: Throwaway ARM template used ONLY to generate a CCE policy via
`az confcom acipolicygen` -- never actually deployed. Named for the
one environment (dev) it mirrors -- infra's own Terraform is laid out
per-environment, so a second environment with different values would
get its own arm-template-<env>.json rather than share this one.
confcom only cares about the container's image/commands/env-var
*rules*, not how the real group gets created (no containerGroupProfiles
support in confcom at all) -- so this mirrors infra's own
aci-session-worker-profile.tf `local.aci_session_worker_container`
definition (that file's own header comment is the authoritative
source for all of this) rather than describing a deployment of its
own. Only `image` and the six environment variables below are
actually load-bearing for what confcom generates -- `cpuCores`/
`memoryInGb`/`location` play no part in the policy at all (confcom
doesn't police resource requests), they're kept aligned with infra
purely so this file doesn't paint a misleading picture of the real
deployment to a future reader. Shape copied from Microsoft's own real
tutorial template
(container-instances-tutorial-deploy-confidential-containers-cce-arm,
raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/confidential-container-demos/
main/hello-world/ACI/arm-template.json) -- the `sku`/
`confidentialComputeProperties` pair is what turns an ordinary
container group into a confidential one; without them the group
deploys but nothing in it validates.
Launch-and-callback design, not the old public-IP/inbound-listener
one this file used to describe: the container has no inbound
listener of its own at all -- it dials OUT to attested-python-
execution's own callback listener over a private VNet path and
presents ACI_CALLBACK_TOKEN. The one declared port (12345, on both
the container and `ipAddress`) is an inert mandatory-port workaround
-- ACI rejects any group with an IP and zero declared ports
(MissingIpAddressPorts); nothing ever listens on it. `restartPolicy`
is hardcoded to Never, not a parameter -- see session_master.rs's own
module doc comment for why Always/OnFailure would silently turn 'run
one session and exit' into an unbounded restart loop reusing the
same confidential container.
`image` defaults to a placeholder -- resolve-image-digest.sh fills in
the real `ghcr.io/directionallyai/aci-worker/aci-session-worker@sha256:...`
reference by digest (never a mutable tag: the CCE policy's own `id`
field pins the same digest, so a tag that moved out from under it
would just make az confcom's policy generation and this template
disagree about which image runs, not any kind of real substitution
attack -- the SNP report's `layers` check is what actually gets
verified at container start).
`ccePolicy` starts empty -- `az confcom acipolicygen -a arm-template.json`
fills it in (and prints its own SHA-256, the value
aci-session-worker-profile.tf's own
aci_session_worker_expected_cce_policy_hash output needs) once
`image` above is a real, resolved digest.
Five env vars below are DELIBERATELY left as unresolved
`[parameters('...')]` references with no default and NO --parameters
file passed to acipolicygen -- ACI_CALLBACK_ADDR/_TOKEN/_GROUP_NAME/
WORKER_EXECUTION_OPTIONS (real per-session values aci_executor.rs's
own create_group() injects at instance-creation time, never declared
on the real profile's own container) and STAYUP_AFTER (a debug-only
value attester-service.tf sets on itself and aci_executor.rs forwards
to the launched worker, same treatment). confcom only emits a
wildcard (re2, .*) env rule when the template value is still an
unresolved parameter reference at generation time -- resolving any of
these to a literal would pin an exact-string-match rule instead,
which would reject every real launch outright since no two sessions
share the same callback address/token/group name. Real incident (see
aci-session-worker-profile.tf's own header comment): an env var
missing from this template entirely isn't a launch failure, it's a
silent drop before the container ever starts
(allow_environment_variable_dropping := true) -- STAYUP_AFTER was
originally left out here and session_master.rs never saw it, no error
anywhere. Keep all five even though none has a real default.
AZURE_ACI_MAA_ENDPOINT is different: it's a real, static value (the
same shared MAA instance attester-service itself already uses),
never per-session -- declared here with its real value rather than
left as a parameter.

metadata.description: Location for all resources -- must be a region where the ACI Confidential SKU is available.

Container image to deploy, pinned by digest -- resolve-image-digest.sh's own output. Never a mutable tag: the CCE policy generated against this template bakes this exact digest into its own `id`/`layers` fields.

AZURE_ACI_MAA_ENDPOINT -- bare hostname, not a URL (get_maa_token() builds `https://{endpoint}/attest/...` itself). Matches aci-session-worker-profile.tf's own real, static value: the shared MAA instance attester-service itself already uses, never per-session.
ACI_CALLBACK_ADDR -- real per-session value, never resolved here. See this file's metadata comment for why it must stay an unresolved parameter reference.
ACI_CALLBACK_TOKEN -- real per-session value, never resolved here. See this file's metadata comment for why it must stay an unresolved parameter reference.
ACI_GROUP_NAME -- real per-session value, never resolved here. See this file's metadata comment for why it must stay an unresolved parameter reference.
WORKER_EXECUTION_OPTIONS -- real per-session value (e.g. "shared"), never resolved here. See this file's metadata comment for why it must stay an unresolved parameter reference.
STAYUP_AFTER -- debug-only value, never resolved here. See this file's metadata comment for the real incident this env var caused when it was left out of an earlier version of this template entirely.
